content: This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is important to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you are using, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements. Share this list with your healthcare provider and pharmacist to ensure safe and effective treatment. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the situation is less critical, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, while Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. If you are using this medication for an extended period, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney function assessments, should be conducted to monitor your health. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to treat and prevent a variety of bacterial infections. Sulfadiazine belongs to a class of drugs known as sulfa antibiotics. It is effective only against certain bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Take this medication orally with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) as directed by your doctor. Unless otherwise advised by your doctor, drink plenty of fluids during treatment to prevent potential side effects. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, or headache. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. In rare cases, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal allergic reactions or other side effects, such as severe skin rashes (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome), blood disorders (e.g., agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia), liver damage, or lung injury. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking sulfadiazine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other sulfa medications, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Sulfadiazine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It should not be used near the expected delivery date due to potential harm to the unborn baby. This drug passes into breast milk. While no harm has been reported in healthy infants, it may have undesirable effects on infants who are ill, premature, or have certain conditions (e.g., jaundice, high bilirubin levels, G6PD deficiency). Breastfeeding is not recommended for infants with these conditions. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
